_meta.purpose: Registry of benchmarks whose grading oracle resolves a semantic convention that the generation prompt does not state, and for which NO frozen decision exists. Wave 3 deliberately made no prompt edit for these (BLOCKED_PENDING_SEMANTIC_DECISION): writing a sentence would have decided the open semantics inside the prompt wave, which the contract forbids. UPDATE (Semantic Interlock wave): every entry now carries a FINAL status; the remaining entries are deliberately ACCEPTED disclosure cases, not pending decisions.
_meta.enforcement_semantics: No automatic sample exclusion and no verdict change. Any downstream stage listed in applies_to that reports per-benchmark results for a benchmark in this registry MUST disclose the open decision alongside the result (e.g. a footnote or column), because a fail verdict on the affected input class reflects an unstated grader convention, not a documented contract violation by the model.
_meta.resolution_path: Each entry names its open decision id. Once a decision is frozen and implemented, the prompt edit (if any) runs as a new atomic prompt wave, the entry is removed, and the benchmark joins the regeneration set of that wave.
_meta.wave3_checker_status: check_prompt_oracle_consistency.py reports all seven benchmarks CONSISTENT on their worked examples; the open decisions concern input classes the worked examples do not exercise (degenerate sizes, boundary conventions, ties, tolerances).
_meta.execution_model_coverage_rule: Wave 3 treated the mathematical prompt semantics atomically across serial/omp/mpi (frozen atomicity rule; benchmarks_partially_changed == 0). An open benchmark-level semantic decision therefore covers all three execution models identically; parallelism_models and prompt_pairs materialize this rule machine-readably (canonical order serial, omp, mpi). prompt_id is derived exclusively as problem_type/name/parallelism_model; array positions are never join keys. Added by the Wave-3 cleanup (2026-08-27, post-commit 730c0afe); enforcement is unchanged: disclosure_required - no automatic exclusion, no suite reduction, no verdict override. The execution-model metadata serves addressability only.

interlocks.unstated_convention: The tolerance regime under which the LU factorization is graded is neither stated in the prompt nor frozen: the oracle-correctness audit records the absolute 1e-3 comparison as potentially unattainable for numerically valid alternative elimination orders (BL-01 / consolidated item #71), and the decision is open (QUEUED - FROZEN IMPLEMENTATION TARGET NOT SPECIFIED).
interlocks.oracle_behavior: cpu.cc::validate() compares against the reference factorization with an absolute epsilon; a differently-ordered but numerically valid elimination can accumulate error past that boundary and be graded fail.
